articles.title: Fantasy Football Week 7 Early Waiver Wire: Omar Cooper Jr. leads group of young wide receivers worth adding
articles.summary: We go over some early options off the fantasy football waiver wire going into Week 7.
articles.body:
By now you've likely settled in with your 2026 fantasy football rosters and know what you have and what needs improvement. We have four teams on bye again in Week 7, with the Bills, Commanders, Chargers and Jaguars not in action. That will create plenty of lineup voids, on top of an ever-growing injury list, forcing you to make some streaming decisions off the wire.

We're here to offer up a few early options as we go into Week 7.

Omar Cooper Jr., WR, Jets (4% rostered on Yahoo)

The Jets got the rookie WR out of Indiana back in the lineup in Week 6 against the Patriots after he missed four straight games with an ankle injury. Cooper's presence was immediately felt with a 6-103-1 line, good for 19.3 fantasy points on the day. Isaiah Williams and Tim Patrick had been playing elevated snaps but that changed with Cooper back, which makes sense given the draft capital invested in the young wideout.

It's unclear when Adonai Mitchell (finger) will return, which bodes well for Cooper operating opposite Garrett Wilson in the Jets offense. We know New York will be in positive passing scripts most weeks as well.

We may not see Cooper do this every week because, well, it's still the Jets. But the talent and opportunity are there, so it may be wise to chase that upside by adding Cooper in deeper formats.

The Texans offense came alive in a tough matchup against the Jaguars in London on Sunday, scoring 34 points in a last-second win. If that trend continues and C.J. Stroud keeps this up, you're going to want a piece of this unit going forward.

Noel has quietly strung together three straight games with double-digit fantasy points, producing 3-85, 5-41-1 and 4-107-1 over that stretch. The volume remains tough to trust but Noel is doing the most with his targets and opportunities, which should help his case for more snaps, even with Marvin Harrison Jr. joining the team. Houston has a winnable matchup against the Giants in Week 7 before the bye, which is tough timing for this pickup. Noel gives you a strong upside flex play.

Travis Hunter, WR, Jaguars (7% rostered)

In continuing our trend of young wide receivers to target off the wire, Hunter had the second best offensive game of his young career in Week 6. Hunter turned four targets into four catches for 59 yards and a TD against the Texans to finish with 13.9 fantasy points. In formats that also count defensive stats, Hunter also had three tackles (one solo), a pass defensed and an interception.

If you're in an IDP league and Hunter is still floating around, grab him immediately. We don't know if this offensive usage is going to continue, but clearly the Jags should make Hunter more of a priority in the passing game. He could become the third/fourth option in an above-average aerial attack.

Similar to Cooper, Hunter is an upside grab off the wire, a player who could pay dividends later after the Week 7 bye.

articles.title: From selling vegetables to Commonwealth medal: Now Jhandu Kumar dreams of Asian Para  Games glory
articles.summary: Kolkata: Not too long ago, Jhandu Kumar used to sell vegetables and drive an e-rickshaw to meet his own expenses and help run the family household.
articles.body: Kolkata: Not too long ago, Jhandu Kumar used to sell vegetables and drive an e-rickshaw to meet his own expenses and help run the family household. Today, the Bihar para-powerlifter is a Commonwealth Games bronze medallist, has secured a government job and is preparing to represent India at Asian Para Games.For Jhandu, who finished on the podium in the men’s heavyweight para-powerlifting event at the 2026 Commonwealth Games with a 190kg lift, the transformation still feels like a dream.“Yes, absolutely. It feels like a dream. A boy from a village who worked hard is now making a name for himself across the country,” Jhandu told TOI from Aichi-Nagoya. “I cannot express how happy I am. Words fail me. Now I have another opportunity at the Asian Para Games to represent my country.”The athlete from Harnaut village in Bihar’s Nalanda district will compete in the 72kg category on Tuesday. He continued his training for the Games at the National Centre of Excellence in Gandhinagar under coach Rajinder Singh Rahelu. More than making drastic changes to his training, he concentrated on strengthening the self-belief that has driven his rise.“The basic approach remains the same. For me, it is about maintaining that inner drive and staying motivated. I have this determination within me: ‘I will do it, I will definitely succeed,’” said the 29-year-old. “That has been my main focus, to perform even better.”However, Jhandu knows there will be little margin for error in a competitive field. Asked what sort of lift could put him in medal contention, he said the numbers alone would not determine the outcome.“A medal could come at 200kg, 205kg or even 190kg. During competition, the mind works differently. You have to manage everything, and there is pressure,” he said. “You have to handle that pressure, and then it depends on how your body responds and how much you can push yourself.”Irrespective of the numbers, Jhandu expects stiff competition and is relishing the challenge. “There are many strong competitors. Lifter from China and Malaysia will be among them, apart from athletes from several other countries. Competition is inevitable. In fact, without competition, it would not be exciting,” Jhandu said.Despite all that he has achieved, Jhandu admits his journey still feels surreal. “Honestly, I never imagined that I would one day compete at Commonwealth Games or Asian Para Games. My focus was simply on working hard and winning a medal for my country,” he said.That hard work has paid off, and the medal in Glasgow did more than establish Jhandu on the international stage. It changed his life back home, too. The reception he received and the support from the Bihar govt, including a govt job, have given him even greater motivation to succeed.None of it, he believes, would have been possible without his family’s support.“My family has always been a huge source of motivation and support. They supported me even when I was selling vegetables and driving an e-rickshaw,” said the para-lifter, who was affected by polio at the age of five. “It is difficult to put into words how much my family has done for me.”The Asian Para Games may be the immediate assignment, but Jhandu already has a bigger destination in mind. “My main target is the Paralympics. I am determined to win a Paralympic medal for India,” he said. “I am prepared to put in whatever hard work is required.”For the boy from a small village in Bihar, the journey that once seemed unimaginable has only made him dream bigger.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Asian Para Games: Mona Agarwal wins gold, Avani Lekhara silver as India clinch 1-2 finish
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India enjoyed a memorable day at the 2026 Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya on Monday as Mona Agarwal won gold and Avani Lekhara claimed silver
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India enjoyed a memorable day at the 2026 Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya on Monday as Mona Agarwal won gold and Avani Lekhara claimed silver in the women's 10m air rifle standing SH1 event.Mona finished with a score of 250.0 points, while Avani came a close second with 249.6 points. South Korea's Lee Yunri won the bronze medal with 227.9 points.The Indian shooters remained in the fight for the top spot throughout the final, but Mona finished ahead of Avani by just 0.4 points to secure the gold medal.The silver medal adds to Avani's record at the Asian Para Games. She had won gold at the 2022 Hangzhou Games and continued her medal-winning run at the 2026 edition.The result gave India a 1-2 finish in the event, with both shooters finishing ahead of the rest of the field.Mona edges Avani in a close finishMona produced a consistent performance in the final to finish with 250.0 points. Avani also put up a strong challenge and ended with 249.6 points, falling just short of the gold medal.The difference between the two Indian shooters was only 0.4 points, making it a closely fought contest for the top two positions.Lee Yunri finished third with 227.9 points to take the bronze medal.Mona sets qualification recordMona had also topped the qualification round with 629.1 points after six series. Her score set a new Asian Para Games qualification record, breaking the previous mark held by China's Zhang Cuiping.She also came close to the world record of 629.4 points, which is jointly held by fellow Indian shooter Avani Lekhara and Slovakia's Veronika Vadovicova.Avani also delivered a strong performance in the qualification round to secure her place in the final before going on to win silver.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ni Mercedes, ni BMW: esta es la marca del coche con más kilómetros del mundo
articles.standfirst: Un conductor estadounidense compró un coche en 1966 y no dejó de conducirlo con regularidad durante décadas hasta alcanzar casi 5,3 millones de kilómetros. Te contamos la historia de este récord
articles.summary: Un conductor estadounidense compró un coche en 1966 y no dejó de conducirlo con regularidad durante décadas hasta alcanzar casi 5,3 millones de kilómetros. Te contamos la historia de este récord
articles.body: Muchas veces los coches pasan de padres a hijos para que estos aprendan... y vayan destrozándolos. Otras, muchísimas menos, el 'afortunado' ejemplar se salva después de haber sido mimado por su primer dueño y caer en manos de un coleccionista. Lo que no es normal es que un coche siga rodando como si nada durante más de medio siglo para acumular un kilometraje del que ni suelen presumir los camiones más veteranos. Pero en esta ocasión no hablamos de un vehículo de trabajo, sino de un coche. Con carrocería coupé, para ser más exactos. La marca en cuestión es Volvo y el modelo afortunado es un P1800 S de 1966. El coche es protagonista de esta historia, pero también su dueño, Irv Gordon, un profesor de ciencias estadounidense que compró el coche cuando tenía 25 años y acabó convirtiéndose en el conductor que más kilómetros ha recorrido con un mismo automóvil, según acredita el Guinness World Records. Gordon se hizo con su Volvo en junio de 1966 por 4.150 dólares, y lo que ocurrió nada más sacarlo del concesionario da una idea de hasta qué punto le gustaba conducirlo: tras recogerlo un viernes y pasar el fin de semana acumulando kilómetros, tuvo que volver al concesionario el lunes siguiente porque ya le tocaba la primera revisión, prevista a las 1.500 millas (unos 2.400 km). Tampoco es que su rutina le impidiera acumular kilómetros, porque cada día recorría unos 200 entre ir y volver de su casa al trabajo. Y así, usándolo todos o casi todos los días, en solo 10 años ya había acumulado medio millón de millas, unos 805.000 kilómetros. Lo llamativo es que Gordon no se propuso desde el principio batir ningún récord. Su primer gran hito llegó en 1987, cuando superó los 800.000 km (500.000 millas), y en 2002 superó los 1.600.000 km (1.000.000 millas), con una celebración en Times Square, en Nueva York. Para entonces, su Volvo ya era una celebridad sobre ruedas. Pero todavía quedaba una cifra que parecía más propia de los recorridos que acumulan los aviones. El 18 de septiembre de 2013, Gordon y su Volvo alcanzaron los tres millones de millas, equivalentes a unos 4,83 millones de kilómetros. El lugar elegido fue la carretera Seward Highway, cerca de Girdwood, al sur de Anchorage, en Alaska. Para la ocasión, el coche viajó hasta allí en un camión cerrado y su propietario llegó en avión. Después de varios días conduciendo por la zona, llegó el momento esperado. No hubo una llegada a toda velocidad ni una celebración espectacular. Gordon explicó que se limitó a circular con normalidad mientras vigilaba el cuentakilómetros para no perderse el instante. Cuando la cifra cambió, el coche había recorrido una distancia equivalente a dar unas 120 vueltas a la Tierra por el ecuador. El propio protagonista resumió que lo importante no era llegar a los tres millones de millas, sino "todos los viajes y las experiencias que le habían llevado hasta allí". Nunca se había fijado como objetivo alcanzar el millón o los dos millones; simplemente "disfrutaba conduciendo". Y siguió haciéndolo. Cuando Gordon murió, el 15 de noviembre de 2018, el contador de su Volvo marcaba 3.260.257 millas, unos 5,25 millones de kilómetros. Es decir, después de superar la barrera de los tres millones en 2013, todavía recorrió más de 400.000 kilómetros con el mismo coche. La respuesta no está en una fórmula mágica ni en un coche preparado para batir récords. El Volvo P1800 S era un coupé de aspecto deportivo que destacaba por un diseño muy reconocible y bonito, pero la clave estuvo también en el cuidado que recibió durante décadas. Gordon era meticuloso con el mantenimiento y utilizó el coche de forma constante, en lugar de guardarlo como una pieza de colección. Eso no significa que todos sus componentes fueran eternos. El motor original continuó en el coche, aunque tuvo que ser reconstruido en dos ocasiones. También se realizaron trabajos de mantenimiento y se renovó la pintura a lo largo de su vida. El mérito no estuvo en que el coche se librara de necesitar reparaciones (excluyendo las dos reconstrucciones), sino en que pudiera seguir funcionando durante tantos años con una conservación cuidadosa. Volvo aprovechó la historia para destacar la durabilidad del modelo y, cuando Gordon superó los dos millones de millas, le regaló un C70. Al llegar a los tres millones recibió otro coche, un XC60. Pero ninguno de esos regalos consiguió apartarlo de su viejo P1800 S. Gordon seguía prefiriendo el coupé rojo con el que había empezado todo. Tras la muerte de su propietario, el Volvo pasó a manos de su hija, Danielle Gordon. Durante un tiempo no estuvo claro cuál sería el destino definitivo del coche, pero la marca terminó adquiriéndolo a la familia para preservar una pieza que ya formaba parte de su historia. Así que, desde abril de 2024, el coche se exhibe en el World of Volvo, el espacio dedicado a la marca en Gotemburgo, Suecia. Allí descansa con sus 5,2 millones de kilómetros en el marcador para demostrar lo que puede suceder cuando se juntan un motor a prueba de bombas, un mantenimiento constante y un propietario que no encuentra ninguna razón para dejar de utilizarlo.

articles.title: All-time great! An Se-young scripts history, ends Susi Susanti’s 29-year reign with record 47th badminton title
articles.summary: South Korean badminton superstar An Se-young has rewritten the history books, becoming the most decorated women’s singles player in international
articles.body: South Korean badminton superstar An Se-young has rewritten the history books, becoming the most decorated women’s singles player in international badminton and ending Indonesian legend Susi Susanti’s nearly three-decade reign at the top.The Olympic champion achieved the landmark with a hard-fought 21-23, 21-14, 21-18 victory over Japan’s Akane Yamaguchi in the Denmark Open final in Odense on Sunday. The triumph took An’s tally to 47 international titles, surpassing Susanti’s record of 46, which stood since the Indonesian great retired in 1997.The Badminton World Federation (BWF) confirmed the milestone, noting that its records, maintained since 1989, exclude titles won at regional games. The governing body hailed the 24-year-old South Korean as “an all-time great”.An’s record-breaking run ends legendary reignSusanti, one of badminton’s most celebrated figures, had held the record for the most international women’s singles titles for almost 29 years. An’s latest triumph has now taken her past the Indonesian icon, underlining her remarkable consistency at the highest level.“I want to make a lot of history and break records but I focus on one match at a time,” An said after her victory, reflecting on the achievement. “That is my motivation. The crowds turn out for me and I’m happy people enjoy every match I play.”The world No. 1 has occupied the top ranking for 105 consecutive weeks, establishing herself as the dominant force in women’s singles badminton. She won a record 11 titles in a single season in 2025 and is building another extraordinary campaign this year.Comeback victory despite ankle scareAn’s record-breaking achievement came after a demanding final against Yamaguchi, who took the opening game 23-21. The South Korean responded strongly to win the second 21-14 and force a decider.The final game presented another challenge when An trailed 11-5 and appeared to injure her right ankle after slipping on the court. Despite the setback, she recovered her rhythm, capitalised on the slower side of the court and completed the comeback with a 21-18 win.“It’s a little bit bad,” An admitted after the match. “The court conditions were difficult and I slipped. I will check my body and talk to my [coaches]. In the final game, I was on the slower side of the court, and I was more confident.”The victory secured her second consecutive Denmark Open crown and ninth individual title of the season.A season of remarkable dominanceAn’s latest achievement adds to a season in which she has won six BWF World Tour singles titles and claimed major honours at the Asian Championships, World Championships and Asian Games, alongside success in team competitions.Her only defeat of 2026 came in the All England Open final in March, where she lost to China’s Wang Zhiyi.An’s rivalry with Yamaguchi has also become one of the defining contests in women’s badminton. The South Korean has now won their last 10 meetings in succession.“I think she’s my best rival. I always want to win against her. She motivates me to train harder,” An said. “Wang Zhi Yi and Chen Yu Fei are rivals too and I’m happy to have them. Rivalry makes you better.”With the record now hers, An has moved beyond chasing individual titles to establishing a legacy that could define an era of women’s badminton.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Asian Para Games: Kapil Parmar bounces back from semifinal defeat to win bronze
articles.summary: India’s Kapil Parmar clinched the bronze medal in the men’s J1 -70kg event at the Asian Para Games after defeating Indonesia’s Rafli Ahnaf Shidqi by ippon
articles.body: India’s Kapil Parmar clinched the bronze medal in the men’s J1 -70kg event at the Asian Para Games after defeating Indonesia’s Rafli Ahnaf Shidqi by ippon in just one minute and nine seconds on Monday.The Paris Paralympics bronze medallist secured India’s third medal on the opening day of the competition, adding another podium finish to his international career.Kapil had earlier booked his place in the semifinals with a victory over Mongolia’s Bat-erdene Baatarsuren in four minutes and 53 seconds. However, he lost to Indonesia’s Junaedi by ippon in the last four before bouncing back to win the bronze-medal bout.Earlier in the day, visually impaired judoka Kokila assured India of its first medal after defeating China’s Yi Liu 1-0 in the women’s J2 -52kg semifinals. Kokila, who won bronze in the -48kg category at the previous edition in Hangzhou, registered one waza-ari and one yuko against her Chinese opponent, who managed one waza-ari. She will now compete in the final.India then secured a one-two finish in the women’s 10m air rifle (SH1) event, with Mona Agarwal winning gold and Avani Lekhara taking silver.Mona, a bronze medallist at the 2024 Paris Paralympics, staged a stirring comeback in the final to set an Asian Para Games record of 250.0 points. She edged compatriot Avani, the defending champion and a two-time Paralympic gold medallist, by 0.4 points, with Avani finishing on 249.6.Mona’s gold also secured India a second quota place for the 2028 Los Angeles Paralympics. She had already earned one quota place at the WSPS World Championships in Changwon, South Korea, last month, where she won silver.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Paola García amplía su palmarés con un oro mundial
articles.standfirst: Es la mejor en la competición sub 21 de katas del campeonato del Mundo en el que España suma ocho medallas, entre ellas, los oros en kumite de Izan Martín (sub 21) y de Candela Peña (cadete)
articles.summary: Es la mejor en la competición sub 21 de katas del campeonato del Mundo en el que España sumaocho medallas, entre ellas, los oros en kumite de Izan Martín (sub 21) y de Candela Peña (cadete)
articles.body: Paola García se subió a lo más alto del podio en las katas del Mundial sub 21, júnior y cadete de Bielsko-Biała (Polonia), un evento en el que España sumó ocho medallas: tres oros, tres platas y dos bronces García se proclamó campeona del mundo sub 21. La extremeña, de 20 años, lleva desde hace tres que combina sus presencias en competiciones absolutas con las de su categoría de edad. Así en 2023 se alzó con el título continental con 17 años tras haber sido subcampeona del mundo junior en 2022 y de revalidar la corona campeona de Europa de esta misma categoría a principios de ese año. En sub 21 había sido campeona de Europa en 2025 y 2026, y segunda en el Mundial de 2024. Ahora ha podido subir a lo más alto del podio en la cita que se ha celebrado en Bielsko-Biala (Polonia). Se impuso en la final a la brasileña Gabrielle Henrique por 3-2 . Este oro se suma este año a la plata continental conquistada en categoría absoluta. El palmarés de Paola García, en categoría absoluta, cuenta también con otros dos bronces continentales y uno mundial, además de dos más en la Premier League (El Cairo 2025 y Roma 2026). Por equipos, cuenta con un oro europeo (2025) y dos bronces mundiales (2023 y 2024). En kumite, Izan Martín se colgó el oro en -75 kg. Se impuso en la final al marroquí Haitam Oufkir por 6-4. El baracaldés ya había sido bronce en el Karate One Series A de Salzburgo hace unas semanas. Este Mundial sub 21 de Polonia también acogió las categorías júnior y cadete. En esta última, Candela Peña también se proclamó campeona del mundo al vencer a la egipcia Jana Kassem por 5-0. El equipo femenino de kata cadete y júnior, integrado por Lucía Rodrigo, Uxía Folgueira, Candela Peña y Rocío Castro, se quedaron con la plata tras perder la final ante Japón que lleva abonado al oro desde 2019. La españolas antes habían ganado a Montenegro, Hungría e Italia. En kumite cadete, Celia Cofrades conquistó la plata en -47 kg, tras caer en la final frente a la estadounidense Victoria Jacoby por 3-1. En júnior, Noa López en -66 kg perdió la final ante la palestina Mariam Bsharat, campeona cadete en 2024, por 3-1. Además, José Ángel León, en kata junior, fue bronce, vía repesca, tras vencer al chino Nuri Wong por 3-2. Julia Just, en kumite sub 21, también pisó el tercer peldaño del podio en -68 kg tras ganar a la neerlandesa Robin Zwanenburg por 2-0.

articles.title: El pádel como arma para el cáncer de mama: "En la pista se me olvidaba que estaba enferma"
articles.standfirst: Diagnosticada en plena pandemia, Mari Garcia Salas, jugadora amateur de pádel, encontró en el deporte un espacio para desconectar durante el tratamiento. Hoy, libre de tumor y todavía bajo seguimiento médico, comparte su experiencia a través de un libro solidario
articles.summary: Diagnosticada en plena pandemia, Mari Garcia Salas, jugadora amateur de pádel, encontró en el deporte un espacio para desconectar durante el tratamiento. Hoy, libre de tumor y todavía bajo seguimiento médico, comparte su experiencia a través de un libro solidario
articles.body: Cuando a Mari García Salas le comunicaron que tenía cáncer de mama, en agosto de 2020, su primera reacción fue mirar a su marido, Jaume, y decirle que iba a superarlo. “Lo voy a superar”, le aseguró. Tenía 48 años, una hija, una familia y una vida en la que el pádel ocupaba un lugar importante. De repente, tuvo que aparcar buena parte de su rutina para centrarse en el tratamiento, en un mundo que, además, permanecía paralizado por la pandemia. Pero hubo algo que intentó mantener siempre que su cuerpo se lo permitió: la posibilidad de seguir entrando en una pista. Mari había empezado a jugar al tenis a los 31 años y descubrió el pádel a los 40, en 2012. Desde entonces, la pala se convirtió en mucho más que una afición deportiva. Por eso, cuando llegó el diagnóstico, hacer todo lo posible por conservar ese espacio también formó parte de su manera de afrontar aquellos meses. "En la pista de pádel se me olvidaba todo, se me olvidaba que estaba enferma”, recuerda. Incluso en los momentos más duros del tratamiento, cuando la quimioterapia ya había dejado su huella en su aspecto físico, llegó a preguntarle a un compañero si se notaba que estaba enferma. Al ver después una fotografía de aquel partido, con el pañuelo en la cabeza y sin cejas ni pestañas, comprendió que era evidente. Pero durante el juego había conseguido dejarlo a un lado. No siempre resultaba sencillo. La fatiga podía ser brutal y hubo ocasiones en las que tuvo que pedir que alguien la sustituyera porque no podía continuar. Sin embargo, mientras se veía con fuerzas para jugar, intentaba no renunciar a esos encuentros. “Ir a jugar durante el tratamiento fue media vida”, explica. No solo disfrutaba mientras estaba en la pista: también prolongaba esa sensación durante los días posteriores, recordando los puntos y reviviendo los buenos momentos. El pádel le aportaba bienestar físico y mental, pero también algo tan cotidiano como tener un partido al que acudir, unas compañeras con las que compartirlo y una rutina que no girase exclusivamente alrededor de la enfermedad. En su caso, además, el deporte siempre ha estado ligado a las relaciones personales. La dimensión social del pádel es inseparable de lo que le aporta: encontrarse con gente, compartir tiempo y sentirse parte de un grupo. Durante el tratamiento, esa combinación adquirió un significado especial. La pala no eliminaba las dificultades ni hacía desaparecer los efectos de la quimioterapia, pero le permitía reservar un espacio para sí misma, más allá de las consultas médicas y de las preocupaciones que acompañan a un diagnóstico de estas características. De aquella experiencia nació también la necesidad de escribir. Mari ya contaba sus aventuras y anécdotas padeleras en su blog, “I need padel”, que había comenzado en 2018. Tras recibir el diagnóstico, recuperó la inspiración y empezó a plasmar lo que iba viviendo: desde el momento en que le comunicaron que tenía cáncer hasta la noticia de que estaba limpia. Lo que inicialmente era una forma de desahogo terminó convirtiéndose en un libro, “I need pádel y a veces quimio”, en el que recoge el proceso con su propia mirada, sin renunciar a las anécdotas, al humor y a los detalles cotidianos. Su intención al publicarlo no era ofrecer una fórmula universal para afrontar la enfermedad, sino compartir herramientas que a ella le habían ayudado. En sus páginas habla de la importancia de centrarse en el presente, de entrenar la mente y de no adelantarse a escenarios que todavía se desconocen. “Cuando tenemos un problema serio, ya sea de salud o de otro tipo, es muy importante tener herramientas o conocerlas”, explica. Le gustaría que una mujer, o un hombre, porque ellos también pueden desarrollar cáncer de mama, que acaba de recibir un diagnóstico encontrara en su libro una lectura amena y recursos que pudiera adaptar a su propia situación. Ahora, seis años después de aquel diagnóstico, Mari puede hablar de una evolución favorable. Su última revisión general, en mayo, confirmó que seguía libre de tumor. No obstante, continúa con medicación y seguimiento médico debido al riesgo de recaída, y está participando en un ensayo clínico que está a punto de cumplir tres años. Su historia no se presenta, por tanto, como un capítulo que se cierra de un día para otro, sino como un proceso que continúa y en el que también hay que aprender a convivir con la incertidumbre. Si pudiera regresar a aquel día de 2020, hay algo que le advertiría a la Mari que acababa de escuchar el diagnóstico: que tuviera paciencia. “El año mientras te curas va a pasar muy rápido y lo vas a llevar súper bien, pero después lo importante es mantenerte enfocada, porque se te va a hacer muy largo”, reflexiona. Porque el final del tratamiento no siempre significa que todas las preocupaciones desaparezcan. También hay revisiones, medicación, efectos secundarios y una nueva forma de relacionarse con el propio cuerpo y con el futuro. En este camino, Mari ha encontrado otra manera de dar sentido a lo vivido: compartir su testimonio en torneos y encuentros solidarios que unen el pádel con la lucha contra el cáncer. Considera que estas iniciativas permiten acercar la enfermedad a un entorno cotidiano, concienciar a quienes practican deporte y recordar que la investigación necesita financiación. Para ella, hablar abiertamente del cáncer es fundamental, igual que lo es dejar de tratarlo como un tema del que cuesta conversar. Hay una precisión en su discurso que resume muy bien su manera de mirar hacia delante. Mari prefiere no hablar de “sufrir” un cáncer, sino de “pasar” por él. No porque reste importancia a lo vivido, sino porque quiere que el lenguaje deje espacio al futuro. Y en ese futuro sigue habiendo pádel, familia, proyectos y ganas de compartir su historia con quienes puedan encontrar en ella algo útil. Su testimonio recuerda que cada persona afronta la enfermedad de una manera diferente y que no existen recetas universales. En el caso de Mari, una pala, una pista y la compañía de otras personas le ayudaron a conservar una parte de su vida en un momento en el que tantas cosas habían cambiado. Hoy, su libro y su compromiso con la concienciación prolongan ese propósito: que su experiencia pueda acompañar a otras personas, que se hable del cáncer con naturalidad y que la investigación siga abriendo caminos. Porque, mientras la enfermedad ocupaba buena parte de sus días, Mari encontró en el pádel un lugar donde volver a pensar en los puntos, en el siguiente partido y en todo lo que quedaba por vivir.

articles.title: Ander Martín y Esther Briz avanzan a octavos del Mundial entre el oleaje
articles.standfirst: Tuvieron que disputar las dos rondas clasificatorias para acceder en una jornada marcada por la irregularidad de las olas con varios vuelcos incluidos
articles.summary: Tuvieron que disputar las dos rondas clasificatorias para acceder en una jornada marcada por la irregularidad de las olas con varios vuelcos incluidos
articles.body: Tras la cancelación e domingo de lo Time Trials por las adversas condiciones meteorológicas en Qingdao (China), este lunes dio comienzo el Mundial de remo de mar en la modalidad de Beach Sprint con Ander Martín y Esther Briz entre los favoritos a las medallas. Los españoles tuvieron que disputar las dos rondas clasificatorias para acceder a las eliminatorias en una jornada marcada por la irregularidad de las olas con varios vuelcos incluidos. Briz, campeona de Europa hace menos de un mes y de la mítica regata Oxford-Cambridge, acabó novena en la primera ronda (3:09.41), dominada por la debutante australiana Isabella Scammell (2:51.92). La remera maña, que comenzó a dar paladas en el Ebro, necesitó acudir al segundo Time Trial, en el que acabó tercera (3:18.25), tras la estadounidense Christine Cavallo (3:05.24) y la neerlandesa Isabel Van Opzeeland (3:17.28). Este martes, en octavos, se medirá a la canadiense Carling Zeeman, sexta en los preliminares. En la categoría individual masculina, Ander Martín, también campeón continental y plata mundial el año pasado en Turquía, fue décimo en la primera ronda de las preliminares (2:45.20). El alemán Moritz Wolff (2:37.09) y el estadounidense Christopher Bak (2:40.29) fueron los mejores. En la segunda, logró el billete a los octavos gracias a su cuarta plaza (2:57.92). Mañana le espera el francés Antoine Lefebvre, quinto en la primera clasificación. El del Real Club Náutico de Torrevieja reconoció en la previa a MARCA que no se fiaba de nadie y podía haber sorpresas, pero también confiaba en sus posibilidades, ya que llega más rápido que nunca a la cita de Qingdao. El cuatro scull mixto de Ignacio Ramón-Borja García, María Ángeles Macián, Alejandra García, Adrián Miramón y Aiunhoa Casanova, superaron la criba inicial con una cuarta plaza, igual que en el doble sculls mixtos Miguel Salas y Teresa Díaz. En sub-19, Xavier Torres fue quinto tras superar al británico Gethin Balkwill. En cuartos se enfrentará a Chun Cai. Por su parte, Marina López, tras un noveno y un segundo puesto, se medirá en cuartos la australiana Maddison McLaughlin En sub-19 doble scull masculino, Manuel Crego y Enrique Martínez, tras una cuarta y una séptima plaza, quedaron fuera de las eliminatorias, en las que sí estarán Sara Torres y Lirios Huélamo, que lucharán ante las griegas Despoina Ermeidou y Eleni Laskaridi, al igual que Alfredo Mena y Blanca López en el doble scull mixto. El doble mixto adaptado de Rocío Fraguela y Marcos Delgado consiguieron el mejor tiempo y están ya en semifinales, en las que se enfrentarán a Annabelle Miller y Justin Stevens.

articles.title: Giants’ John Harbaugh, Cam Skattebo give media conflicting answers on RB’s zero carries
articles.summary: Reports emerged on Sunday morning that the New York Giants would remove running back Cam Skattebo from the starting role for the team’s game against the New...
articles.body:
Reports emerged on Sunday morning that the New York Giants would remove running back Cam Skattebo from the starting role for the team's game against the New Orleans Saints after the second-year ball-carrier fumbled four times this season.

As was reported, Najee Harris went on to start at running back for the Giants and finished with four carries for two yards in a 34-27 Giants loss.

Skattebo, on the other hand, played just six snaps and didn't get a single carry.

After the game, Skattebo admitted that he was "punished" by the coaching staff for his fumbling issues.

"I got punished for what I did," Skattebo told the media. "I understand it, so I gotta be ready when Coach calls my name, and that wasn't today."

"I didn't expect to have zero (carries)," Skattebo added. "I was expecting to not play as much… It's hard, but I've made mistakes, and I got to own up to them."

But Giants head coach John Harbaugh claimed that the team "didn't bench" Skattebo and that the zero carries were "not by design."

"It wasn't by design for him not to carry the ball," Harbaugh said. "It's just, when he was in there, we didn't call any runs."

After Harbaugh tried to elaborate on the reasoning and how the Giants were looking for someone among the running backs to step up as "the guy," he got snippy with the media.

"I think it's been pretty clear, the whole story. I don't even know what else to say," Harbaugh explained. "That's the best answer you can ever get on that in a thousand years. There's not a coach in the world that will give you a better answer than that. If you're not thrilled with that answer, I got nothing else for you. Honestly."

Harbaugh can spin it however he wants to, but it's clear that Skattebo is in the doghouse and was more or less benched. Skattebo had 81 carries over the Giants' five games entering Sunday.

The Giants' three other running backs — Harris, Tyrone Tracy Jr., and Devin Singletary —combined for 34 yards over 14 carries (2.4 yards) in the loss. So, Harbaugh and the Giants might have to accept the fumble risk from Skattebo in an effort to try to get the running game on track going forward.

articles.title: Matt Campbell Remaining Committed to Rocco Becht
articles.summary: "Insanity is doing the same thing over and over again and expecting different results." This popular metaphor isn't the clinical definition of insanity, but...
articles.body:
"Insanity is doing the same thing over and over again and expecting different results." This popular metaphor isn't the clinical definition of insanity, but some fans would argue that insanity is Matt Campbell keeping Rocco Becht as Penn State's starting quarterback.

Matt Campbell Remaining Committed to Rocco Becht

The Michigan loss was another dreadful showing by the senior quarterback. Becht completed 28-of-44 attempts for 267 yards, one touchdown, two interceptions, and fumbled once. All three of Becht's turnovers resulted in touchdown drives in the 21-18 loss .

Becht has gone through rough patches throughout his five-year college career, but none as bad as this. Iowa State notably went on a four-game losing streak in 2025, during which Becht threw for 1,016 yards, four touchdowns, and five interceptions. This year, Becht has thrown for 913 yards, three touchdowns and five interceptions during this current four-game losing streak.

Still, Campbell has not considered changing quarterbacks.

"Man, how that guy continues to compete and fight and gave us a chance, even at the end of the football game," said Campbell after being asked if there was any consideration of benching Becht. "He's got to be better. He will continue to grow and be better. But no, there's never any consideration from my end. "Matt Campbell Remaining Committed to Rocco Becht

Is Campbell's Loyalty Costing Penn State Games?

Becht and Campbell have been tied at the hip since Becht became the starter at Iowa State in 2023. Together they won 26 games and made a Big 12 Championship in Ames. The loyalty to Becht is understandable, and it was supposed to be a strength for this team.

"I've always felt that the quarterback and the head football coach have to be tied at the hip. And I've felt that they have to be tied at the hip because their leadership is so critical to the entirety of the football program," Campbell said in February.

But that loyalty appears to be costing Penn State games. Not much has improved since this losing streak began. Last week's one-score loss to USC looked like a small step in the right direction ; Becht threw for a season-high 289 yards, one touchdown and no turnovers, but it clearly didn't carry over. Instead, Becht had his second multi-interception game of the year and has yet to break 300 passing yards in a game.

It feels like Penn State is doing the same thing over and over again and expecting different results by keeping Becht as the starter.

"I feel free. I feel good. There are just some plays that aren't there for me. They just don't work out for me," Becht said. "I get unlucky. That happens. It's humbling."

What Does Penn State Have in Alex Manske?

Much has been said about backup quarterback Alex Manske 's athleticism, yet he hasn't seen the field. Offensive Coordinator Taylor Mouser said before the season that Manske "is one of the most talented guys on the offense" and that "we're not going to be able to keep him off the field this year." But Manske hasn't appeared in a game since non-conference play.

So what's the deal? Why has there been no interest in giving Manske a shot? Look at what Michigan did. Former No. 1 recruit in the nation, Bryce Underwood, was benched at halftime for true freshman Tommy Carr , and it worked. But it might not be that simple in Happy Valley.

Nate Bauer of Blue White Illustrated said on BWI Live postgame that Manske may not be as game-ready as originally anticipated.

"I had a check-in of some variety internally with the program; people who have seen practice. And the sentiment was, 'eh, you don't want to see Manske,'" Bauer said.

Bauer did not specify when this check-in occurred. He did say, however, that the program is frustrated with Becht, but ushering Manske into the starting role isn't as simple as it sounds.

"Internally, Penn State football could not be more frustrated than it is with Rocco Becht, and that's before [the loss to Michigan]. So fans, your frustrations are absolutely shared," Bauer said. "… if it were as simple as plugging the other guy in, I do think that they would do that because they are trying to win football games. Any amount of loyalty that you think, as a fan, Matt Campbell has toward Rocco Becht, Matt Campbell would give that away to win football games. I feel very confident in that."

Penn State seems to be stuck between a veteran quarterback who can't get the job done and an athletic redshirt freshman who isn't fully ready for Big Ten play. At 3-4, the Nittany Lions still have a shot at becoming bowl-eligible, though recent performances indicate that this is unlikely, even if there is a quarterback change.

articles.title: Fornaroli secures McLaren race seat for 2027 in pivotal career move
articles.summary: Leonardo Fornaroli will return to competitive racing in 2027 after McLaren confirmed the Italian as part of their Hypercar driver line-up for the World Endur...
articles.body:
Leonardo Fornaroli will return to competitive racing in 2027 after McLaren confirmed the Italian as part of their Hypercar driver line-up for the World Endurance Championship. The reigning Formula 2 champion will take part in the British team's new endurance racing project, which includes an appearance at the 24 Hours of Le Mans, while retaining his position as a Formula 1 reserve driver.

The announcement gives Fornaroli a new opportunity to race regularly following a year spent working behind the scenes with McLaren's Formula 1 operation. The Italian joined the team's setup after securing the 2025 Formula 2 crown, adding to the Formula 3 championship he won the previous season.

Throughout 2026, Fornaroli contributed to McLaren's Formula 1 programme through simulator work, testing and development duties. He also made appearances in official practice sessions at the Spanish and Hungarian Grands Prix, gaining further experience in Formula 1 machinery. However, he did not contest a full racing championship during the season.

His new commitments will see him balance two different programmes in 2027, continuing to support McLaren's Formula 1 team while preparing for the challenges of endurance racing in the Hypercar category.

Fornaroli reacts to McLaren's Hypercar announcement

Fornaroli welcomed the chance to take on a new challenge with McLaren, explaining how his existing Formula 1 responsibilities helped create the opportunity to compete in the WEC: "Joining the McLaren Hypercar Team is an incredibly exciting next step in my career and I'm grateful that my role as McLaren Mastercard Formula 1 reserve driver has opened up this incredible opportunity," Fornaroli said.

"I'm delighted to be continuing in that role next year while also taking on this new challenge. To represent McLaren in the FIA World Endurance Championship and at the 24 Hours of Le Mans is a huge honour, and I am ready to give everything as we take on this new challenge together."

The 2025 Formula 2 champion also highlighted the contribution of McLaren's driver development structure to his career, having progressed through the junior categories before securing his place within the organisation.

"I'd like to thank the McLaren Driver Development Programme for supporting me throughout my journey and for giving me the opportunity to develop my skills on such a competitive and prestigious stage."

Barclay explains why McLaren selected Fornaroli

McLaren Hypercar Team Principal James Barclay believes Fornaroli's performances in Formula 3 and Formula 2 demonstrate his potential to make an impact in endurance racing, despite his limited experience in the discipline.

"Leo is an exceptional talent: winning Formula 3 is a significant achievement, but to follow that by winning Formula 2 as a rookie underlines his natural talent and one of the most exciting drivers in motorsport," Barclay explained.

"His speed, consistency and maturity at such a young age helped him achieve a huge amount in the junior categories and those same attributes make him an exciting addition to our McLaren Hypercar Team."

Barclay also explained that his earlier experience with the Italian played a part in his positive assessment of the signing: "We have a great driver lineup forming, which blends experienced sports car drivers and now young talent for our debut season. I worked with Leo briefly in my previous role and his approach and performance impressed me very much, we both look forward to taking on McLaren's debut season in the World Endurance Championship together."

articles.title: Pirates Top Prospects No. 13: Johan De Los Santos Joins Brother on List
articles.summary: This is one in a series of stories breaking down PBN’s Top 30 Pirates prospects. It was a family reunion […]
articles.body:
This is one in a series of stories breaking down PBN's Top 30 Pirates prospects .

It was a family reunion for Johan De Los Santos when the Pirates signed him out of the Dominican Republic for $2.25 million in 2025. He joined the same organization as his older brother, Yordany, who ranks 20th on our top 30 prospects list.

The younger De Los Santos shined in his first professional season in 2025. In 44 games in the Dominican Summer League last year, he slashed .353/.451/.460 with nine doubles, three triples, 27 RBI and 34 steals.

De Los Santos began the 2026 season in the Florida Complex League and again played well. He batted .310/.431/.434 with four triples, two doubles, 10 RBI and 26 steals in 31 games. The 18-year-old also played in 21 games with Low-A Bradenton, where he posted a .218/.258/.310 batting line with three doubles, one triple, one home run, nine RBI and 13 steals.

De Los Santos used his speed to combine for 39 stolen bases this season, the third-most for any Pirates' minor-leaguer. In addition to his above-average speed, he also has an above-average arm.

De Los Santos has split his time up the middle between shortstop and second base. He's played 47 games at shortstop in his minor-league career with a .940 fielding percentage and 44 at second with a .977 fielding percentage.

De Los Santos hardly strikes out. He's only gone down on strikes 37 times in 405 career trips to the plate. He's also drawn 54 walks during that time and has had more walks than strikeouts in each of his first two seasons.

The 5-10, 165-pound De Los Santos focuses on a line drive approach at the plate and possesses keen eye. His frame suggests there won't be much home run power as he develops.

De Los Santos, who doesn't turn 19 years old until next July, is still raw but has some appealing traits and looks like one to watch as he develops in the system.

articles.title: Liverpool Reportedly Out: Chelsea Target ‘Dead Set’ on Joining Blues
articles.summary: Despite it being October, the transfer mill never truly stops spinning with clubs seemingly already lining up their business for January and beyond. Liverpoo...
articles.body:
Despite it being October, the transfer mill never truly stops spinning with clubs seemingly already lining up their business for January and beyond. Liverpool have started their season under Andoni Iraola fairly well, new reports indicate they won't look to strengthen certain areas in the winter window, which could open the door for Chelsea to swoop in and make a move happen. Let's dive into the different reports that could change the campaign for either side if they're proven right.

Liverpool Could Miss Out on Chelsea Target As They Wait for Summer

Based on a joint report from the Athletic's Stuart James & Thom Harris, with some additional details from David Ornstein, the Reds are not prioritising the addition of a midfielder in January. Their current outlook is to wait to see the development of Trey Nyoni and James McConnell. It is noted that this could change in January, presumably based on departures or a lack of development from their younger players.

This was all in regards to Alex Scott, with the report making it clear Liverpool are interested in the midfielder, but not for a January move. They would be more interested if things dragged on to the summer when they could make a clearer decision.

It is noted in the aforementioned report that Bournemouth could want up to £100 million to allow Scott to move in January, with Chelsea named as the current front runners to make a move in the winter. Having sold Enzo Fernandez on deadline day, the Blues didn't have time to line up a replacement and went into the campaign light in the middle of the park. While Jordan Henderson has hit the ground running, he is a short-term option at 36. Add in the surgery to Reece James sidelining him and they are looking at a few months with just four senior midfielders.

Simon Phillips, a Chelsea reporter of many years, today spoke about the Cherries midfielder. He indicated that Xabi Alonso and some players have already contacted Scott about a move. Phillips believes that the Bournemouth man will be "dead set on joining Chelsea", with no word as to whether that will be in January or the summer.

Reports from both the Liverpool side and Chelsea side currently have the Blues leading the charge to sign the highly-touted midfielder. If a transfer is on the table in January, it looks most likely that Scott will be headed to London. This would help complete the side, offering a great partner to Moises Caicedo and someone who can long-term fill the role that Henderson has occupied. The big question now will be the fee and whether it goes above £100 million or not.

articles.title: Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes equals a rare Tom Brady career milestone
articles.summary: During his postgame press conference, Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes opened up about equaling a rare Tom Brady milestone | @EdEastonJr
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes spoke with reporters after the Week 6 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers. He opened up about equaling another rare Tom Brady career milestone.

"My honest first reaction is they've said this from 97 on. I'm like, 'When did Tom (Brady) lose another game?' Because I feel every game I win, I tie him (laughter)." said Mahomes, "But in all seriousness, in all seriousness, it's always an honor to be in any conversation as far as winning football with him. That's the GOAT. He knows how to win football better than anyone really in any other sport. And so, if you can be mentioned in any category with him, it's special."

Mahomes tied Brady for the fewest starts (131) to reach 100 wins, adding another strong comparison to the legendary quarterback.

"As I've gone throughout my career, I think I've gotten better and better at winning. You know, it's not always pretty. It's not always how I want it to be," said Mahomes. "I want to throw three touchdowns, four touchdowns, and I want to put up big stats, but whenever your defense is playing like they are today, you can't force it. And after I forced that one early in the game, I just said, 'Hey, let's figure out the best way to win the football game,' and we were able to do that."

Mahomes threw for 272 passing yards and one interception in the Chiefs' 22-6 win on Sunday at Arrowhead Stadium.

"I'm a little more disappointed in Hadribeaj corner. Here you have a guy working his butt off, trying to keep this guy off of him, using these tactics, and you see him putting his feet on the ropes trying to get some rest and you still don't bring the stool in to get this man off his feet. That's the inexperience that I just didn't like.

"He was doing good from the first couple of rounds and then it just started declining because you see Fundora picking up the pace…But to credit Fundora, he did what he had to do but at the same time, I would like to see more.

"He's getting hit with those overhand lefts, overhand rights, and he's not throwing the right hook. I'm saying 'where's the right hook.' This guy did not throw the right hook one time and he's going to need that if he fights those guys like Boots and Vergil."

articles.title: Giants RB Najee Harris admits confusion over RB situation after Cam Skattebo benching
articles.summary: The New York Giants stumbled against the New Orleans Saints in a 34-27 loss on Sunday, with the decision to bench running back Cam Skattebo intensified specu...
articles.body:
The New York Giants stumbled against the New Orleans Saints in a 34-27 loss on Sunday, with the decision to bench running back Cam Skattebo intensified speculation surrounding the team's backfield hierarchy. Najee Harris, who started in Skattebo's place, expressed confusion about the team's approach after receiving limited opportunities in the loss.

Skattebo entered the game under pressure after fumbling four times during New York's first five games. Although he received a few snaps versus New Orleans, he was not given a single carry. Harris instead opened the game as the starting running back but finished with just four rushing attempts for two yards across 11 snaps.

The 28-year-old acknowledged that the Giants' frequent substitutions made it difficult to build momentum and identify the best ways to exploit the opposing defense.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"It's hard to get in a rhythm with one or two plays," said Harris postgame. "The first couple runs will be like, 'OK, how are they playing it?' And then the next ones will be, 'OK, this is how you attack it.' But if you're getting a play here and then get taken out for a series, there's nothing you could do. That's why I'm saying, 'I don't know.' I've never been through none of this before."

Harris was not the only New York running back who found success hard to come by against the Saints. Tyrone Tracy Jr. and Devin Singletary also failed to provide a consistent ground threat, with the team's three active running backs averaging just 2.4 yards per carry combined.

The Giants' rushing woes continued despite facing a New Orleans defense that allows the seventh-most yards per rush. Right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor's absence because of a calf injury added to the offensive line's problems, which had shown shortcomings in opening running lanes over the past five games.

New York attempted different offensive approaches, including formations featuring fullback Patrick Ricard and blocking tight end Chris Manhertz, as well as five-receiver sets. However, those adjustments produced little success after the team opened the game with a 12-play, 93-yard touchdown drive.

The defeat also featured a major offensive collapse. After taking a double-digit lead, the Giants surrendered 34 consecutive points, with turnovers and stalled possessions contributing to the Saints' surge.

New York eventually responded with 17 unanswered points during the final 11 minutes after quarterback JJ McCarthy replaced Jameis Winston . However, McCarthy's fourth-down pass intended for Isaiah Likely fell incomplete in the end zone with 12 seconds remaining.

The loss dropped the Giants to 3-2-1, while New Orleans improved to 2-4. New York will next visit the Houston Texans in Week 7, who have won their last two games after beginning the season 0-4.

articles.title: Midseason report card grades for USC football secondary
articles.summary: If the Trojans' leaders in the secondary can take it up a notch, the defense will be a lot more formidable in the second half of the season
articles.body:
USC football's biggest struggles on defense stem from its secondary. The explosive plays given up this season all come from the secondary's poor play. The Trojans will need their veterans to step up, along with the further ascent of some of their young guys.

Here is my midseason report card for the Trojans' secondary after the first seven weeks of college football:

Pierce is the consistent leader of the Trojans' secondary. He has 39 tackles and 1 interception for the season so far. Although the secondary has struggled a lot at times, Pierce has been that bright spot and the player who has stepped up. In the big games, you can rely on him to make big plays. This unit will continue to follow his lead, and if he keeps playing well, that will go a long way.

Kennedy Urlacher, in the games the Trojans have won, has had a huge impact. Urlacher has 3 sacks this season, proving he is amazing in blitz situations. He has 21 tackles and 1 forced fumble to add to his great production to start the season. Urlacher is a weapon for the Trojans' defense. I am excited to see him take off further the rest of the season.

Alex Graham has not been as consistent as Urlacher, but he is finding his rhythm as of late. He can make contributions beyond just his coverage skills. Like Urlacher, he has also proven he is reliable in blitz situations. He and Urlacher have both helped elevate the Trojans' pass rush. He has 15 total tackles, 3 tackles for a loss, and 2 sacks so far. He is an underrated X-factor for the Trojans' defense, getting better as the year goes on.

He has had some good moments in coverage. However, the Trojans haven't gotten that elite corner from Iowa State, which had 4 interceptions. That is the player this Trojans defense needs desperately. If they can get one more guy to step up alongside Christian Pierce, the Trojans' defense would be just fine. He has not been the biggest reason for the Trojans' struggles in the back end, but it is time for him to be the main reason USC's secondary turns the corner in the second half of the season.

He has been the Trojan who has generated the most turnovers in the secondary. The veteran corner has 2 interceptions, one of which was a 99-yard return for a touchdown. He changed the momentum of the Rutgers game with his big play. The Trojans will need a lot more of that in their upcoming stretch of games. So far, Brown has been a nice player in the rotation this season.

Chasen Johnson is a young corner who has been getting a fair opportunity. However, he has been learning a lot this season. It has been more ups than downs for him in coverage. In a few games, opposing offenses have attacked him. His struggles this season will make him better in the future, but his play will improve if the veterans set the tone first.

Elbert Hill is another young guy who has gained experience in the big games and had a great chance to learn in his freshman season. In the first few games, he flashed; against Oregon, he got challenged. He will not make this secondary elite this season, but in the next few years he will be a nice building block.

RJ Sermons has been the most impressive young player from this unit this season. He has shone on special teams, and when his number gets called, he goes out there and makes plays. He makes his money on special teams, and it seems like he stands out every week in that regard. RJ Sermons is a player USC should feel confident is heading in the right direction.

articles.title: Raiola bounces back with his redemption
articles.summary: Dylan Raiola steals the show against Nebraska.
articles.body:
Oregon Ducks quarterback Dylan Raiola struggled last week and was benched. He got a shot at redemption against a school he once called home: the Nebraska Cornhuskers.

Raiola was benched last week, losing his starting spot to third-string quarterback Brock Thomas. His play suffered, costing the Ducks a home loss in a ranked Big Ten showdown. He was granted a second chance on Saturday.

With Dante Moore still on the injury report, the Ducks have struggled to find consistency at quarterback over the last three weeks. Thomas and the Ducks offense were scoreless in the first half.

Thomas was 9-of-20 for 54 yards and threw an interception, and the offense had only scored six points before being pulled.

Raiola entered the game in the fourth quarter to start for Oregon with a 14-6 deficit. The offense came alive when the third-year quarterback took over. He led them downfield to score the game-winning touchdown, the Ducks' only touchdown of the game.

Raiola finished the game completing 11-of-19 passes for 59 yards and a touchdown.

"I love Nebraska, that's my home. My first two years there, it was home. I love the fans, I love everybody there, but it was about Oregon tonight," Raiola said in his postgame interview.

Moore still has no official return date, but if he can't play again in week 8, will Raiola be the number one guy again?

Oregon hits the road to play Illinois on Saturday, October 24 (3 p.m. ET).

articles.title: F1 Fan Shares How Ocon Saved Her From Severe Anxiety Attack and Still Remembers Her
articles.summary: An F1 fan shares a tale of how Esteban Ocon saved her life after she suffered a severe anxiety attack at the airport in 2023. After Haas announced the depart...
articles.body:
An F1 fan shares a tale of how Esteban Ocon saved her life after she suffered a severe anxiety attack at the airport in 2023.

After Haas announced the departure of Ocon at the end of the 2026 season, eventually replacing him with Ferrari F1 junior Rafael Camara , a fan of the Frenchman shared a tale from her life that she had not spoken about on a public platform.

She dates it back to the 2023 season, when she was at the airport for Ocon 's arrival for the Hungarian GP. She describes what she remembers from the brief memory that another fan pushed her way to greet Ocon for photos and autographs.

In doing so, that person hurt the fan to the extent that she suffered a severe panic attack at that moment. She recalled hurting her ribs and falling unconscious, but hearing Ocon in the background, who was asking if she was okay.

She noted that Ocon did not leave until she was okay and fully conscious, even requesting the security personnel to call an ambulance if needed. However, she refused and was fit enough to leave on her own with her friends.

After a few days, she visited an emergency physician, and she was diagnosed with severe anxiety, aside from the ribs issue. The nurse noted that if not for the assistance from Ocon, she would have had to spend a night in an emergency room.

She wanted to share this tale to help F1 fans understand a different side of a driver. With some fans disregarding the Frenchman post his non-contract renewal, she came out in his defense – not forcing her opinion, but showing a different side.

In fact, she revealed that Ocon remembers her to this day, and whenever they happen to meet – largely at the Hungarian GP – he enquires about her health. She feels grateful, as she thinks the Frenchman gave her a second life.
